items.title: A call statement that is exactly 100 columns before its `;` is left on one 101-column line: the Call arm measures `first_line_over_budget` before the `;` is pushed, while a chain statement of the same width splits
items.body: `let value = plain_function_call_with_no_chain_at_all(argument_one, argument_two, aaaaaaaaaaaaaa);` inside a function (tab = 4 columns) is 100 columns without the `;`: the statement hook arms the split (the whole statement is 101), but the Call arm's own measure (E314/E321) sees 100 and keeps the arguments inline. The same width as a three-link chain splits at its links. Unchanged since E314 (hole-only); E321 makes it reachable outside markup. Fix: the Call arm counts one column for the statement's terminator when the call is the statement's tail (or carries the armed split's knowledge that the statement overflowed). Sizing XS.

items.title: A two-operand binary whose right operand is a call (`a == b + 1 && starts_with(write.path, held.path)`) breaks the CALL's arguments one per line while the `&&` stays inline: `&& starts_with(` ... `)`
items.body:
E321's refusals cover chains of three or more operands; a two-operand chain has no operator split (E147's threshold), so the call's arguments are the only break left and the result reads `let a_key = x == y + 1 && starts_with(
	write.path,
	held.path,
);` (std reactive/store_core.vl, two sites). Accepted with the layout; alternatives: refuse the call-in-a-2-operand-chain too (the line stays long, as before E321), or let a 2-operand `&&`/`||` chain break at its operator when its right operand is a call. Owner's taste.
